evidence.requirements: Every point in the brief is met. The start page lists title, date and time, price and "<n> seats left" (TastingCard.tsx:23-40, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingCard.tsx:45-47). The form has Name, Email and Guests (1-8) fields and a Book button (BookingPage.tsx:112-126), and errors show under their field (form.jpg). The server rejects bookings above seats left (store.ts:57-58). The confirmation shows the heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, with the password taken from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:11, StaffPage.tsx:56-65). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (store.ts:78, staff.jpg). Built with React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. Bookings live in memory, PORT defaults to 3000, and the UI is in English.
evidence.correctness: Capacity is checked and inserted synchronously (store.ts:53-72), and a test sends 6 parallel requests (app.guest.test.ts:69-76). Seats left are always derived from the stored bookings, so cancelling frees them. Bounds 1 and 8 are accepted; 0, 9, 2.5, '1e1', NaN and null are rejected (booking-schema.test.ts:32-41). Unknown tastings return 404, and a fully booked tasting replaces the form with a notice (BookingPage.tsx:41-53). Two flaws: Overview calls the parent's setState during render when the session has expired (StaffPage.tsx:76-77), a React anti-pattern that triggers warnings. After a 409 'only 1 seat left' error, the Availability box on the left still shows the stale count (BookingPage.tsx:102).
evidence.security: The password check hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual, and an empty or unset password never matches (password.ts:6-8). Session tokens are random 256-bit values with a TTL, stored in memory (sessions.ts:21). The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, with an optional Secure flag (app.ts:102-108). Logout destroys the server-side session. Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:87-94). helmet sets a CSP; the API requires JSON content type, limits bodies to 10kb and handles parse errors. React escapes all output, and no secrets are in the code. One small gap: the rate limit is per IP and trust proxy is not set, which the README admits (README.md:54).
evidence.code_quality: The layout is clear: shared zod schema, catalogue and format used by both server and client; createApp with injectable store, clock and TTL; a small store and session module; focused React components (TextField, Alert, TastingCard). Naming is clear, the API returns typed result unions and errors are handled consistently (client.ts, app.ts:140-145). Points off for the side effect during render (StaffPage.tsx:77) and the hand-rolled useAsync that disables the exhaustive-deps lint rule (useAsync.ts:21-22).
evidence.tests: Tests cover every layer. Unit: schema boundaries, store capacity, cancel and references. API (supertest): validation, 409 seat limit, concurrency, 415, 413, 400, login, rate limit, sessions, expiry, logout, auth on staff routes. Components (Testing Library): field errors via accessible description, server errors mapped to fields, fully booked state, network error, staff cancel and expired session. Playwright e2e: full guest and staff journeys, axe WCAG audits, and a phone viewport with no horizontal scroll (journeys.spec.ts, phone.spec.ts). Coverage thresholds are 80%, and the last run passed (test-results/.last-run.json).
evidence.ux_design: Each screen has a clear hierarchy. In form.jpg the summary sits beside the form, and the error appears in red with a tinted field background directly under Email. confirmation.jpg uses a green success panel with a checkmark and a neat summary table. The Book buttons are clear and the seats-left counts are colour-coded. A fully booked badge and notice exist in code (TastingCard.tsx:17). Weaknesses: Cancel is immediate with no confirmation, and the start page has no imagery or details about what each tasting includes, which a winery site would usually show.
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a label tied to it with htmlFor. Errors are linked through aria-describedby and the field gets aria-invalid (TextField.tsx:14-21). Focus moves to the first field the server flagged (BookingPage.tsx:78). Alerts use role=alert or role=status (Alert.tsx:18). The page has semantic article, section, dl and table markup with scoped headers. The staff Cancel button is described by the booking reference (StaffPage.tsx:169). Focus outlines are visible, buttons are at least 44px tall, and the HTML has lang=en. Playwright runs axe WCAG 2.2 AA audits on every page (journeys.spec.ts:124-144). Contrast in the screenshots looks adequate.
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies match the job: Express, helmet, express-rate-limit, cookie, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, Tailwind and Fontsource. There is no database or state library, and the in-memory store is about 80 lines. The code is compact for the scope, with no needless layers.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers run, env vars, test commands, folder layout and assumptions, and package-lock.json is present. Missing: there is no CI pipeline config at all. README.md:47 points to openspec/ for requirements, design and tasks, but openspec/specs holds only a .gitkeep, so the documented decisions are not there. engines is ">=22" with no .nvmrc, so the runtime is not pinned. There is no changelog or release approach beyond version 1.0.0. Staff guidance is limited to one README line.
evidence.visual_design: The palette fits a winery: wine red, cream and parchment, with a green accent for success. The type pairing (Fraunces display serif with Inter) is consistent on every page, and spacing and rounded cards are uniform (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, staff.jpg). It looks finished and polished. It is still fairly generic: there is no photography, and the grape mark is small, so it reads as a template more than a distinct winery identity.
evidence.layout: The most important content comes first. The intro sits above a three-column card grid in start.jpg. The form uses two columns, summary and form, in form.jpg. The confirmation is centred in confirmation.jpg. Staff bookings are grouped into header cards with tables, and seats left appear in each header (staff.jpg). The screenshots show no overlap or clipping. The staff table collapses into labelled rows on phones (StaffPage.tsx:143-149), and phone e2e tests check there is no horizontal scroll.
evidence.usability: Booking takes three steps: start page, form, confirmation. Labels and buttons use the brief's wording, typed values are kept when errors appear, and a '1 to 8 guests' hint is shown. Staff stay signed in across reloads, get a success notice after cancelling and can sign out. Cancel is a one-click, permanent delete with no confirmation (README.md:55), so a misclick loses a guest's booking. After a seat-limit error the availability box shows stale numbers.
evidence.reception: Guests would trust it: it looks professional, is on-brand and gives a clear confirmation with a reference. Staff get a clean overview. It loses a little because it gives little detail about the experience (no description of each tasting) and sends no email confirmation, though neither is required.

strengths: Every requirement in the brief is met, and capacity is enforced server-side with synchronous check-and-insert, tested under 6 parallel requests
Strong security: constant-time password comparison, random expiring server-side sessions, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict cookie, login rate limit, helmet CSP, JSON-only bodies with a size limit
Thorough tests at every layer (unit, supertest API, Testing Library, Playwright e2e with axe audits and a phone viewport), plus a polished, consistent winery look in all four screenshots
issues: Maintainability gaps: there is no CI pipeline, the README points to openspec requirements and design docs that do not exist (openspec/specs has only .gitkeep), and the Node runtime is not pinned (engines ">=22", no .nvmrc)
Staff Cancel permanently deletes a booking in one click with no confirmation (StaffPage.tsx:166-173, README.md:55), so a misclick loses a guest's reservation

Smaller correctness issues: the parent's setState is called during render when the session expires (StaffPage.tsx:76-77), and after a seat-limit error the form's Availability box shows a stale count (BookingPage.tsx:102)
review.verdict: This is a complete, secure and well-tested booking app that looks polished and fits a family winery; every requirement in the brief is met. Before handing it over, I'd add a CI pipeline, either add the design docs the README promises or remove the claim, pin the Node version, and add a confirmation step to Cancel.
